title: Orchestration RBAC Evidence Playbook
body:
Overview:

This playbook guides on-call responders through collecting and enriching evidence when role grants originate from orchestration systems and SIEM events are incomplete. It focuses on quick containment, ensuring forensic fidelity, and reconciling RBAC state so that security, infra, and devex teams can triage and remediate safely.

Key assumptions:
- SIEM may have truncated nested arrays (actor.roles).
- There exists a raw audit bucket with gzipped JSONL shards retained for 90 days.
- The policy engine can emit evaluation traces when requested.

First 15 minutes (triage & containment):
- Acknowledge alert and create incident ticket (INC-YYYY-###).
- Record the triggering rule and alert text, capture event_id and timestamp.
- Identify actor_id and immediate resources impacted; revoke tokens/sessions for that actor if feasible.
- Cordon orchestration worker nodes or pause the job queue to prevent further grants.

Evidence preservation (must-do):
- Copy raw audit shard(s) covering +/- 2 hours from the event to an immutable S3 path under s3://redwood-sec-incidents/INC-YYYY-NNN/artifacts/.
- For each file copied, compute and store sha256 digests in a manifest file.
- Snapshot current RBAC policy repo (git head and last 30 commits) and place in artifacts.

Enrichment steps (fast method):
- Run enrichment parser: tools/enrich_audit_stream.py --in <shard.gz> --out enriched.jsonl.gz --preserve-arrays --schema-tag audit_v2.
- If actor_roles fields are missing, query policy-eval traces using policy_trace_id if present; otherwise request a targeted trace from the policy engine using the exact event payload.
- Cross-reference orchestration logs (k8s audit, job controller, image digests) to confirm the actor context.

SIEM export guidance for responders:
- When exporting evidence to SIEM, include schema_version and an attachments pointer if nested arrays are large.
- Do not rely on SIEM document alone for forensics; include raw shard pointers in the incident ticket.

RBAC reconciliation quick commands (examples):
- Dump evaluated grants: rbac-tool dump --format json > rbac-eval.json
- Compute diff against templates: rbac-diff rbac-eval.json templates/ > rbac-diff.txt
- Search for wildcard grants: jq '.grants[] | select(.pattern|test("\\*"))' rbac-eval.json

Short-term fixes to apply during incident response:
- Patch templating library to block implicit wildcard expansion and roll the change to the templating service.
- Add explicit approval requirement for orchestration-originated elevation requests.
- Update SIEM ingest mappings to attach schema_version and preserve attachment pointers.

Post-incident follow-ups (owners):
- Security to add audit_schema_v2 emitter changes to runtime (owner: Kenji Watanabe) with target date 2025-01-15.
- DevExp to implement a pre-merge linter for templating patterns (owner: Olga Petrov) with target date 2024-12-20.
- Infra to implement attachments-backed ingest mapping in SIEM (owner: Diego Morales) with target date 2024-12-10.

Hunt queries samples for investigations:
- role.assign AND actor.roles.keyword: "*admin*"
- token.create AND actor.type: "orchestration" AND token.ttl:>3600
- sequence detection: role.assign THEN secret.access within 10m window

Contacts and escalation:
- Security on-call channel: #sec-oncall
- Pager duty alias: sec-pager
- For suspected lateral movement or active exploitation, escalate to Incident Commander and SRE lead immediately.

Appendix: evidence items to always include in ticket:
- Raw shard pointers and sha256 manifest
- Enriched JSONL and enrichment tool version used
- RBAC policy repo snapshot (git head) and evaluation trace pointers
- Orchestration job manifests and image digests

If assistance is needed to run enrichment tools or obtain policy traces, message the security on-call channel and reference this playbook and the incident ticket.
